operation_details.item: The user uses Google Fonts as one of their type sources.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Hey, hope you had a good weekend. I'm finalizing the type stack for the Thompson brochure. I'm pulling a few web fonts from Google Fonts for the secondary text, but the main display type is a foundry license I just logged.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Sounds good! I thought you mainly use Adobe Fonts for client work. What made you go with Google Fonts for this one?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Mostly load time and the specific character set. I still use Adobe Fonts for most projects, but sometimes Google Fonts has a lighter option. For display faces, I buy direct foundry licenses, and all client typefaces are logged in the license tracker.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Got it. So the license tracker has the foundry ones, but do you track the Adobe and Google fonts too, or only the paid ones?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I track everything that's used on a client deliverable, including Adobe Fonts and Google Fonts. The tracker just needs the source and the usage rights. That way I can verify at a glance.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That's a solid system. By the way, did you see the new variable fonts from that foundry we were discussing? Might be a good display option for the next project.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I did! I actually have a couple of them in my test project already. I'll check if they're worth buying direct — if so, I'll add them to the license tracker and maybe use Adobe Fonts for the body text as usual.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Perfect. Let me know if you need any help with the brochure layout after you lock the type. I can review the hierarchy while you finish the visuals.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Forget only that I use Google Fonts as a type source, while keeping the Adobe Fonts, foundry, and license tracker details.
